_note: The safety markers the doctor's Triage screen draws beside each reading, and the one place their alert lines are kept. Founder instruction, 2 October 2026: make triage visual, mark each reading good or bad, and use standard readings for the demo that an officer can change and review later. So this file is the officer's: every number in `lines` may be changed here, by the Clinical Governance Lead, and nowhere else. The green edge is not here: in range means inside the indicative adult range in packages/catalog/records.json#observations, which the nurse's assessment, the Passport and the Protocols table already read, so a reading cannot be in range on one screen and out of it on another. What this file adds is the line past which an out-of-range reading is marked for action now. A marker draws a clinician's eye to a reading; it is not a score, it is not added up, it is not adjusted for age, pregnancy or medication, and nothing in MyThuso decides, escalates or notifies from it.

governance.source: Adult bands adapted from the Royal College of Physicians' NEWS2 chart (2017) for pulse, breathing, temperature, oxygen and low blood pressure; the hypertension guideline's 180/110 for very high blood pressure; and the 3.0 and 14.0 mmol/L lines for very low and very high glucose.
governance.banner: Demo thresholds. These lines are standard adult defaults chosen for the preview and have not been reviewed by the Clinical Governance Lead.
governance.why: A line that decides whether a reading is drawn red is a clinical decision, and it belongs to a named role under a date. Until the role is filled and the review is written here, every screen that draws a marker says the lines are demo defaults, and a check fails the build if this file claims a review without a reviewer and a day.

markers.label: Outside range
markers.meaning: Outside the indicative range but short of the alert line. Look again and read it beside the rest.

markers.label: Past the alert line
markers.meaning: At or past the alert line. A clinician should see this reading now.

markers.label: No reading
markers.meaning: Nothing has been recorded for this measure.

linesNote: Inclusive: a reading equal to a line is past it. `null` means the measure has no alert line on that side — oxygen saturation cannot be dangerously high on room air. Each line must sit on or outside the edge of the indicative range in records.json; where one touches the edge, as low systolic does at 90, a reading on it is past the alert line, because the line is the more cautious of the two. The build checks it.

screen.intro: Every reading for the patients in the sandbox, marked against the indicative range and the alert lines. The markers point a clinician's eye. They decide nothing.
screen.boardNote: Ordered by the most urgent marker on the patient's latest readings, then by name. The order is a reading aid; who is seen first is a clinician's call.
screen.noConsent: No reading is shown. This patient has not agreed to their readings being shared with the care team.
screen.whereNote: The alert lines are packages/catalog/triage-markers.json, changed by the Clinical Governance Lead. The green band is the indicative range in packages/catalog/records.json, the same one the nurse's assessment and the Passport read.

preview.why: Fictional readings for the three sandbox patients in packages/thusoiq/fixtures.ts, taken minutes ago, so the board has something to mark. One is calm, one has chronic readings to watch, and one has a fever with a fast pulse. The third patient has not consented, so the screen shows the refusal instead of their readings — and none are written here for them.
